_comments.devDependencies.jsdom: Root has no tests of its own - this exists only so npm hoists jsdom to the same node_modules level as the shared vitest package. Without it, vitest's internal bare import('jsdom') can't resolve (extension's jsdom devDependency stays nested instead of hoisting), silently dropping the 2 jsdom-environment test files from extension's suite. Do not remove as 'unused'. See commit 95951c5.
_comments.devDependencies.ansi-styles: Same class of hoisting problem as jsdom above, hit 2026-07-24 after a clean node_modules reinstall (needed to make the ws override below actually take effect): @testing-library/dom's nested pretty-format needs ansi-styles@^5.x, but the only copy npm placed anywhere in the tree was wrap-ansi's incompatible v4.x, so pretty-format's own `require('ansi-styles')` failed and every jsdom-environment popup component test (TradeTabWired.test.tsx, CheckTab.test.tsx) errored at collection time. Pinning a 5.x copy here forces npm to hoist one both can see.
_comments.optionalDependencies: Workaround for npm's optional-deps lockfile bug (npm/cli#4828): a package-lock generated on Windows records ONLY win32 native binaries, so `npm ci` on the Linux CI runner can't load rollup/esbuild/rolldown and every vitest/vite step fails (CI was red from 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-14 because of this - the same class of bug could resurface for rolldown, added 2026-07-24 when vite 8 introduced it as vite's primary bundler, so it's listed defensively even though this lockfile already resolved it correctly on its own). Listing the Linux x64 binaries as direct optional deps forces them into the lockfile on every platform; npm skips installing them locally on Windows. Versions must track rollup's, vite's bundled esbuild, and rolldown's own pin (rollup 4.x/esbuild 0.28.x/rolldown 1.1.x for vite 8) - `npm ls rollup esbuild rolldown` when bumping.
_comments.overrides.ws: 2026-07-24 security pass: @ethersproject/providers@5.8.0 pins ws@8.18.0 exactly, vulnerable to GHSA-58qx-3vcg-4xpx / GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p (both fixed in 8.21.0+). Scoped to @ethersproject/providers (not blanket) because @walletconnect/jsonrpc-ws-connection independently pins ws@^7.5.x (a different major, never affected by these two CVEs) and forcing that one to 8.x too would be an untested, unrelated major bump for WalletConnect's own relay connection. 2026-08-05 correction: the original 3-level-nested form ("@polymarket/clob-client-v2": {"@ethersproject/providers": {"ws": ...}}) silently never applied - `npm ls ws` kept showing 8.18.0 under providers even after a from-scratch reinstall, despite this file claiming 'verified' since 07-24. Flattened to 2 levels; confirmed via `npm ls @ethersproject/providers` there's exactly one copy in the whole tree (all 3 paths to it dedupe to the same 5.8.0), so scoping directly to the package (not the grandparent) is still precise, not a blanket override, and now actually takes effect.
_comments.overrides.protobufjs: 2026-08-05: @xenova/transformers@2.17.2 -> onnxruntime-web@1.14.0 -> onnx-proto@4.0.4 pins protobufjs@^6.11.2, vulnerable to 11 advisories incl. GHSA-xq3m-2v4x-88gg (critical, arbitrary code execution) - none fixed in any 6.x release. `npm audit fix --force` only offers downgrading @xenova/transformers to 1.4.2, which is NOT a fix, it's a regression (older than what's installed). Blanket override is safe here - `npm ls protobufjs` shows exactly one consumer chain in this whole tree (onnx-proto, used only to parse the .onnx model's protobuf schema at load time - never touches user/network input). Verified byte-for-byte: forced to 7.6.5 (first patched 7.x release) and re-ran the pinned MiniLM-L12-v2 model - embeddings identical to the last float digit vs unpatched 6.11.6, confirming protobufjs 7.6.5 decodes the same .onnx bytes into the same graph. Migrating off @xenova/transformers entirely (to its successor @huggingface/transformers) was investigated and rejected for now: v3's dtype/quantization API changed, recommended models moved to a different HF org, and in Node it defaults to the native onnxruntime-node binding (which failed to load at all in a real test here) instead of the portable onnxruntime-web/WASM this project relies on for a zero-install npx package and a portable CI cron job - a real migration project, not a dependency bump.
